input.quote: 15.15 Rights Reserved. No license or any other right is granted to either Party, by implication or otherwise, except as specifically set forth in this Agreement. All rights not exclusively granted to SFJ are reserved to PB and its Affiliates.
input.rationale: This funding agreement contains no vendor-to-customer licence grant to police: rather than licensing IP to us, SFJ leaves us in ownership. PB retains sole and exclusive ownership of all Existing PB Intellectual Property (11.1.1.1(a)), owns all Trial Inventions outright regardless of inventorship (11.1.1.3(a)), and acquires sole and exclusive ownership, even as to SFJ, of the Trial Data Package and all Research Results (11.1.1.4); Section 15.15 reserves all rights not expressly granted to SFJ to "PB and its Affiliates". Ownership is broader than the preferred licence position — it is perpetual, cannot be revoked at SFJ's discretion (no "revocable" or at-will termination language appears anywhere), and is inherently exercisable by our affiliates and by contractors acting on our behalf. Section 15.6 also lets either Party assign, sublicense or transfer the Agreement and all of its rights to an Affiliate or to a successor "in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise", which satisfies the successor/M&A transfer element without any consent requirement. Third-party contractor rights are also directed to us on freely-assignable, multi-tier sublicensable terms (11.1.1.3(c)). The only structural point worth noting (not a deviation) is that SFJ holds the Trial Data Package until the purchase/assignment trigger, but the Research Results are deemed PB's Confidential Information with PB as disclosing Party, so our use is unrestricted in the interim. No redline is warranted; flagging this would only weaken a bargain that already benefits us.
